original_question: For a system consisting of a single impurity interacting with identical fermions through the wide-resonance Hamiltonian, prove or disprove that, for fixed mass ratio m/M and scattering length a, there is an upper limit on the number of fermions that can belong to a stable non-Efimovian bound state with that impurity, either in vacuum or with a Fermi sea present.
target_in_paper: In section II.3.2, the authors ask: “Perhaps, from the theoretical point of view, it is more interesting to ask the question: could we prove the existence of an upper limit (with Fermi sea present or in vacuum) to the number of fermions in a non-Efimovian bound state with a single impurity for given mass ratio m/M and interaction parameter 1/(k_Fa)?”
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the system (single impurity interacting with identical fermions via the wide-resonance Hamiltonian), the fixed parameters (mass ratio m/M and scattering length a), and the core open problem (existence of an upper limit on the number of fermions in a stable non-Efimovian bound state, in vacuum or with a Fermi sea) as stated in the paper.
missing_details: Specify the system is three-dimensional at zero temperature and defined by the wide-resonance Hamiltonian (Eq. (1)) with contact s-wave interactions and cutoff taken to infinity
Define k_F as the Fermi wave vector of the background gas when considering the Fermi sea case, and introduce the dimensionless parameter 1/(k_Fa)
Clarify the regime “non-Efimovian,” i.e. m/M and 1/(k_Fa) below the threshold for Efimov trimer formation [m/M<13.384…]
Define “stable bound state” to mean an eigenstate with energy below all decay thresholds into smaller subsystems, ignoring deep bound states
State explicitly that the question permits both vacuum and finite density (Fermi sea) cases, each parameterized by m/M and 1/(k_Fa)
Reference the Hamiltonian’s definition (Eq. (1)) and the wide-resonance assumptions (scattering length and interparticle spacing much larger than effective range)
Quantify that the question asks for a proof or disproof of the existence of an integer N_max
Note the zero-temperature assumption and the grand-canonical ensemble when a Fermi sea is present
refined_question: Consider the Hamiltonian H of a single spinless impurity of mass M interacting via s-wave contact interactions of scattering length a with a three-dimensional ideal Fermi gas of identical fermions of mass m at zero temperature (the wide-resonance, zero-range model of Eq. (1)). Let k_F denote the Fermi wave vector when a Fermi sea is present, and define the dimensionless interaction parameter 1/(k_Fa) for the gas case (or equivalently a for the vacuum case). For fixed mass ratio m/M and fixed interaction parameter (a in vacuum or 1/(k_Fa) with a Fermi sea), does there exist a finite maximum integer N_max such that no non-Efimovian bound state of the impurity with N>N_max fermions can be stable (i.e., have energy below all decay thresholds) in either vacuum or immersed in the Fermi gas? Prove or provide a counterexample.
justification: The refined question preserves the paper’s exact open problem (II.3.2) while supplying all necessary context and definitions to make it self-contained. We include the system’s dimensionality, zero-temperature condition, Hamiltonian reference, scattering model assumptions, definition of non-Efimovian regime, stability criterion, and the role of k_F for the Fermi sea case. This specification aligns precisely with the notation and scope used by the authors and avoids broadening beyond the paper’s intent.
